findings.issue: The only two tests that prove the recovery actions do real work pass by GLOBAL TEST POLLUTION, not on their own merit. aggregateDiffFindings.issue: Two user-facing affordances with no implementation behind them, both reachable by a real click in the shipped desktop app: 'Retry' (handler is `= Unit`) and 'Locate adb...' (side effect posted into MirrorHost's default no-op onSideEffect). 5244 lines were added in this spec; these are the only two places where the UI promises something the code cannot do. See AF-1, AF-2.

One of four ViewModel test classes omits the module's own `useTestDispatcherForOrbit` harness call. The pattern is established in MirrorFakes.kt with a KDoc explaining exactly why it is mandatory ('Orbit defaults both dispatchers to real thread pools ... without this the reducer runs off the test scheduler and advanceUntilIdle() returns before any state has changed'), and the three sibling classes follow it. The omission is invisible in a full-suite run because Orbit.configureDefaults is process-global - the sibling classes fix it for this one. Any test class relying on another class's global setup is order-dependent by construction.

Result handling is inconsistent across the ViewModel's use-case calls. `boot()` inspects the Optional and posts BootFailed on failure; the two new recovery handlers discard theirs. Same layer, same monad, opposite treatment, and the silent half is the one on an error-recovery path. See AF-11.

NO DEFECT FOUND - recorded because it is the spec's one trust boundary and I checked it adversarially. A user-chosen path arrives from outside the program and is executed. It is validated by REUSE of the single `isExecutableFile` predicate (`File(path).isFile && canExecute()`) that every ordered candidate passes through, not by a second validator that could drift; a missing path, a directory or a non-executable file falls through to the ordered list instead of erroring. No raw-argv or raw-String escape hatch was added to data-device-api (its CLAUDE.md forbids it, and `git diff` confirms HostCommand gained only parameterless cases). `grep -rln ProcessBuilder --include="*.kt" . | grep -v /build/` still prints exactly one path. Four ToolResolverTest cases cover the valid-wins, unusable-falls-through, cache-bypass-on-clear and adb-only paths.

THE ESCALATION LADDER IS GENUINELY CORRECT AND GENUINELY COVERED - this is the claim I attacked hardest and it held. I applied six mutations to DeviceRepositoryImpl.kt / DeviceCommandException.kt and every single one was killed, each file restored byte-exact afterwards:
(a) delete `if (!failure.isTimeout()) throw failure` in listDevicesEscalating (heal on ANY failure) -> `a non-timeout failure spawns nothing and is reported as it is` FAILED. So a parse error or a non-zero exit really does spawn ZERO processes.
(b) remove healDaemon's escalation to restartAdbServer() -> `a start-server that times out escalates to kill-server then start-server` + `a daemon that will not come back reports the real reason and keeps polling` FAILED. So a timed-out startServer really does escalate to killServer-then-startServer.
(c) swap restartAdbServer's order to start-then-kill -> `restartAdbServer kills the daemon before starting it` + two more FAILED.
(d) remove healDaemon's own timeout guard -> `a start-server that fails for another reason is not treated as a wedge` FAILED.
(e) turn the second listDevices attempt into a 3x retry loop -> `a failed poll is reported and the next tick polls again` + `a failed poll does not advance the empty poll escalation` FAILED. So there really is exactly ONE escalation per poll and no loop.
(f) reduce isTimeout() to `exitCode == null` -> `timeoutFailureIsDistinguishedFromAParseFailure` FAILED (data-device-api).
Structural checks that back this up: TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX has exactly one producer (ProcessRunner.kt:85, built from the constant, not hand-typed) and one consumer (isTimeout), so rewording cannot silently disarm the ladder; the withdrawn pre-emptive start-server is genuinely absent from the code, not just from the KDoc; healDaemon's inner exception propagates out through poll() to the loop's catch, so a second failure becomes PollFailed and the next tick starts over. Carry-forward 2 was also honoured properly - DeviceDiscoveryPollingTest.kt:468 builds the watchdog text from DeviceCommandException.TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX, and MirrorViewModelDiscoveryTest.kt:172-177 deliberately uses a NON-watchdog reason with a comment explaining that presentation renders reasons and never classifies them. THE ONLY GAP IS THE RECORD, NOT THE COVERAGE (AF-9): no mutation or RED run for these tests is written down anywhere, while TEST-NAME-MAP.md and commit 4269a73 both claim they were proven.
